unit: g/day or mmol/day, see each budget

budgets.title: Where glycine goes: net metabolic uses (adult, 70 kg)

items.label: Collagen synthesis (net of recycling)
items.note: Assumes 95% of glycine released in the procollagen cycle is recycled; at no recycling the gross need is 240 g/day; low = supply-matching 4 g/day (recycling >98%).

items.label: Other protein synthesis (net)
items.note: Turnover 203 g/day non-collagen protein, ~5% glycine; 1 g/day net is the authors' value, high = gross 10.2 g/day (calc).

items.label: Creatine synthesis
items.note: 7.3 mmol/day (3.7-14.6) x 75.07; Meléndez-Hevia Table 2 uses 5.6 mmol = 0.42 g. Neutral for glycine in that author's one-carbon accounting because the methyl group is made from serine.

items.label: Purines
items.note: A net glycine SOURCE overall in that accounting (+0.21 g/day).

items.label: Hippurate (benzoate conjugation)
items.note: Not in Meléndez-Hevia Table 2; diet dependent.

items.label: Bile acid conjugation (net, de novo)
items.note: Gross conjugation is ~0.45 g/day (6 mmol; Hepner 1972) but the freed glycine is largely oxidised after bacterial deconjugation.

contested: The headline "10 g/day deficit" = items 15.2 g/day (this list, with hippurate) minus 5.15 g/day supply = ~10 g/day; the authors' own balance is -8.5 to -10 g/day with 14.5 g/day of uses.
Collagen need (the biggest item) rests on a 95% recycling assumption and on net collagen synthesis of 96.5 g/day assembled from rat, rabbit and human tissue data.
Tracer-derived de novo glycine synthesis (7-44 g/day in four studies, see glycine-synthesis-estimates) is 2.5-15x the 2.9 g/day pathway sum; no study has directly tested the deficit.
No study measured whether 3-10 g/day oral glycine changes collagen turnover.

budgets.title: Five estimates of endogenous glycine synthesis (NOT additive)

items.label: Meléndez-Hevia 2009: summed pathway fluxes (net new glycine)
items.note: Only net new glycine; counts one-carbon units used.

items.label: Yu 1985: de novo N-synthesis, low-N diet 0.6 g protein/kg
items.note: 59 vs 20 umol/kg/h with vs without dispensable amino acids; the no-DAA value is the 2.5 g/day end.

items.label: Tan 2022: de novo synthesis, fasting, healthy weight
items.note: 124 (IQR 103-159) umol/kg lean mass/h at an ASSUMED 50 kg lean mass (my assumption).

items.label: Robert 1982: post-absorptive de novo synthesis
items.note: 81% of 240 umol/kg/h flux = 194 umol/kg/h.

items.label: Gersovitz 1980: fed, 1.5 g protein/kg/day
items.note: 351 umol/kg/h of 458 umol/kg/h flux; falls sharply on 0.4 g/kg protein.

contested: The estimates measure different things (net pathway sum vs tracer rate of appearance that includes recycling through serine and one-carbon exchange). Both Gibson 2002 (glycine production maintained on marginal protein) and Tan 2022 are cited against a hard shortage but neither quantifies a deficit.

budgets.title: Gross whole-body glycine flux and its tracer-derived partition (fed adult, 70 kg)

items.label: Glycine cleavage system (decarboxylation)
items.note: The [1-13C] tracer in the later study gives about half (96 vs 190 umol/kg/h).

items.label: Protein synthesis, glutathione, creatine and all other uses (remainder)
items.note: Remainder 463 - 193 - 190 = 80 umol/kg/h; the ranges of the three parts are wide enough that it could be zero.

contested: This is turnover (appearance and disappearance), dominated by recycling through protein breakdown, serine exchange and the cleavage system; it is NOT net synthesis or net requirement. Fasting flux is 240 umol/kg/h (30 g/day).

budgets.title: Where body choline comes from (adult, 70 kg)

items.label: Dietary choline (free + phosphocholine + GPC + PC)
items.note: US 338 mg/day, Framingham 313, EU 291-468 mg/day. Only ~8% of US adults meet the AI.

items.label: Endogenous de novo choline moiety (PEMT)
items.note: PEMT SAM use divided by three. Inherits the 2-fold PEMT uncertainty.

contested: Rat de novo choline synthesis (70 umol/day per 100 g, Wise & Elwyn 1965, as extrapolated in Meléndez-Hevia 2009 to ~49 mmol/day for 70 kg) is inconsistent with a total methyl budget of ~20 mmol/day (3 SAM per choline) and was NOT used.

budgets.title: What happens to body choline (adult, 70 kg)

items.label: Oxidised to betaine, then DMG, sarcosine, glycine (CHDH/BADH)
items.note: Inferred from urinary sarcosine in patients with a sarcosine-oxidation defect (Mudd 1980/2007, second-hand). Betaine -> methionine by BHMT donates one methyl group per betaine to the methionine cycle.

items.label: Gut-bacterial trimethylamine (urinary TMAO)
items.note: ASSUMED: 5% (1-30%) of dietary choline. A large free-choline bolus gives 63% (Zhang 1999); phosphatidylcholine does not raise TMAO (Cho 2020).

items.label: Acetylcholine synthesis
items.note: Whole-body ACh turnover NOT FOUND; shown as a token so the bar is complete.

items.label: Residual (net PC/membrane accretion, urinary choline/betaine, faecal loss)
items.note: Remainder of the midpoint supply; not measured. Renal clearance of betaine is <5% and ~4% of an oral betaine dose is excreted unchanged (Lever 1994; Schwahn 2003).

contested: The partition is NOT measured as a whole in humans. Isotope studies give enrichment ratios, not fractions of dose (Yan 2013: d9-betaine:d9-choline 1.24; d9-PC 9.4%, PEMT-derived d3/d6-PC 0.17 of d9-PC).

PEMT share of hepatic PC synthesis: 20-40% of the CDP-choline rate in rat hepatocytes, ~10% in mouse (Pynn 2011), up to 47% in mouse hepatocytes vs ~10% in human liver cell lines (2026 NMR, not in repo). Human in vivo: not measured.
Pregnancy diverts choline toward PC and away from betaine (plasma choline +30%, betaine/DMG/sarcosine -13 to -55%; Yan 2012).
